title: mcp: query_records and get_record say which fields field-level security withheld, so an answer says "not visible to you", not "blank"
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a child of the cross-lane parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic), filed on the maintainer's word in this session's chat, 2026-11-18, verbatim: 「开源项目能做的尽量在开源项目做，云端等开源项目完全优化好再开工」, given in answer to this session's analysis of the hosted card on this defect.

## Why

A member asks for a value they are not allowed to read, their own cost rate for example. The answer says the field is blank. Nothing leaks, and the person is misled: they conclude the data is missing and go and fill it in, or report a bug. The hosted product fixed this for its own agent; a client on the open MCP door still gets the misleading answer.

Who acts: the server lane (`packages/mcp`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, a read of `packages/plugins/plugin-security`). Reader: every MCP client asking on behalf of a user with a restricted field.

## Evidence

- The framework strips an unreadable field from every row it serves and leaves no marker: `FieldMasker.maskRecord` deletes the key (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/field-masker.ts:448`), and selecting a hidden field in `fields` is not refused. A row therefore cannot tell withheld from empty.
- Objectstack main (read 2026-11-18): no `withheldFields` anywhere in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` or `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`.
- The hosted product measured the misleading answer on its ask set (a member's own cost rate read as blank) and fixed it in its own tools: its record tools return `withheldFields` and a note. That fix does not reach the open door.
- On the open door the misleading answer is inferred from the code above; it was not reproduced there.

## Scope

- `query_records` and `get_record` results carry `withheldFields`: the fields the call asked for, or the object declares, that field-level security withheld from this caller's rows.
- **The bound, which is the security line of this card:** only a field the caller's own served schema shows is ever named. A field removed from the caller's schema is never named, in this list or anywhere in the result. The framework's own answers decide both, asked as the caller; nothing is derived by comparing rows.
- The same member on `aggregate_records` when a withheld field was asked for as a measure or a group, if the door does not already refuse it.
- A short note in the result: these fields exist and are not visible to you; say so, never say they are empty.
- HTTP and stdio alike. The ask-data skill and the served text gain one line.
- Pins: a withheld field named; a field hidden from the schema not named; an empty readable field in neither list.

## Done when

- On an example app with a field restricted for a member persona, a question about that field over MCP is answered "not visible to you", and the scenario ask round carries that question (#35113).

## Out of scope

- Any change to what field-level security withholds. Write paths.

## Relations

- Parent: #34659. Same pattern as #34919 (a result member the hosted product computed in a wrapper, moved into the framework for both doors).
- Security-touching: yes. It changes what a tool result says about a field a caller may not read. The bound above is the one the hosted fix adopted; widening or narrowing it is the maintainer's to say.
- Dedup, open and closed: the search this card was filed with found no card.
